notes: Algo now markets this unit as the "8180 IP Audio Alerter" (G2) on its site, though it is widely sold/known as the "8180 SIP Audio Alerter" — same device. Desktop/wall-mount unit (7"x4"x2.6", 1.0 lb) with a snap wall-mount bracket; not rack-mountable, so rackUnits omitted. Power is delivered entirely via PoE over the single RJ45 jack — there is no separate power/DC connector. Ethernet speed (100 Mbps) confirmed via the 8180 (G2) User Guide LED description (docs.algosolutions.com), not the main product spec page, which omits port speed. The three analog I/O functions (external speaker, line output, relay in/out) are documented as living on a shared terminal-block strip, but Algo's public spec sheet never names the connector family (e.g. "Euroblock/Phoenix"); "euroblock" was chosen as the closest listed connector type for a captive-screw terminal block — verify against the physical unit or installation guide diagram if exact part number matters. Built-in omnidirectional talkback/ambient microphone is internal (not a physical connector) and so is not listed as a port. Could not access B&H's spec table directly (403 blocked) to cross-check against a retailer source.

ports.name: Network
ports.note: Single RJ45 jack; carries SIP/network traffic and receives PoE (IEEE 802.3af Class 0, 48V, up to 15.4W draw at the source / 12.95W device max). User guide: 'an RJ45 jack for network connection'; amber LED confirms a successful 100 Mbps link.

ports.name: Speaker Output
ports.note: Captive screw/terminal-block output for an external 8Ω horn or ceiling speaker(s), 8W; connecting it disables the internal 3" driver. Exact connector brand/pitch not stated by Algo — modeled as euroblock (closest listed terminal-block type).

ports.name: Line Output
ports.note: High-impedance line-level output, nominal 0dBm into 600Ω, for driving an external amplifier. Shares the same terminal-block strip as the other I/O; connector type inferred as euroblock.

ports.name: Relay I/O
ports.note: Dry-contact terminal that is field-configurable as EITHER a supervised NO/NC input (compatible with Algo 1202/1203/1204 accessories or an EOL resistor) OR a relay output (max 30V, 50mA) — the two functions share the same physical pins and only one is active at a time. Modeled as bidirectional because the pins themselves are user-assignable, not because signal flows both ways simultaneously.
